rv.q: The Lightning Thief makes a personable and accommodating companion.
But truth ain’t really in the building here: the show can’t drop the broad strokes when the material most demands something more.
You may flinch at the dorkiness, but if you’re in the mood to join in and let the t.p. fly, there’s fun to be had.
But platitudes like "The things that make you different make you strong" only reinforce the impression that Y.A. musicals need something extraordinary to make it to the adults' table.
Any parents who shell out that kind of money for this tacky, bargain-basement production seriously need to reevaluate their financial priorities.
The current version, which opened at the Longacre Theater on Wednesday after a seven-month national tour earlier this year, has all the charm of a tension headache.
The current version feels padded, especially for young theatergoers who already know the story.
But the overstuffed goodies of the performances come with a price.

Like Riordan, the team behind Percy Jackson knows and frequently charms its audience—even if its call to fight the darker creatures that lurk within and outside us has been delivered many times with more imagination.
The Lightning Thief: The Percy Jackson Musical, a show thin on substance and thick with trendy teen angst, was not the best candidate for said transformation.
But the monsters don’t seem that scary, and Percy never seems that in danger.
The production looks so cheap visually that let’s be kind and not name the designers.

cn.t: Critics find this YA adaptation energetic but underwhelming, with most deeming it better suited for regional theater than Broadway. The show earns points for liveliness but lacks memorable songs and theatrical magic.

vs.sum: The Longacre Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, even from the balcony, and the sound quality is consistently praised. While the seating is a bit narrow, it provides average comfort for most patrons. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant Beaux Arts interior, and facilities are typical for a Broadway venue, with some lines at intermission but generally manageable.

acc.note: Small restroom-only elevator (may not accommodate all wheelchairs). 3 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra.
